title: Gaia XP H-alpha emission of 132 TESS CPV hosts is the same as that of matched young rapid rotators; a mean circumstellar excess above about 0.7 A is excluded
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips from material near corotation. Time-series spectra of two CPVs showed H-alpha emission from corotating plasma clumps, with 10-60% of the stellar equivalent width (EW). We tested at population level if CPV hosts have more H-alpha than other rapid rotators. We used the Gaia DR3 H-alpha pseudo-EW from RP spectra, which is averaged over 2014-2017, for 117 hosts and 1,706 non-host rapid rotators of the TESS sector 56-107 survey, and for 15 hosts and 761 non-hosts of sectors 1-55. We calibrated the Gaia scale with spectroscopic EWs of 1,307 nearby M dwarfs (0.039 nm per A in active stars). At fixed colour only, hosts emit 2.9 +/- 0.6 A more. This excess is youth: at fixed colour, age class, period and height above the main sequence, the host offset is +0.23 A (95% -0.70 to +1.16 A; positive means less emission). Inside 1-200 Myr groups it is -0.13 +/- 0.53 A without the height term. Sixteen variants give -0.39 to +0.84 A, matched controls give +0.5 A (permutation p = 0.38), and the residual distributions agree (KS p = 0.26). Thus a mean circumstellar excess above about 0.7 A (12% of typical rapid-rotator H-alpha) is excluded, and a 3.6 A emitting state fills at most 19% of the host time if non-hosts have none. Host H-alpha does not follow dip amplitude. Either bound plasma is common to young rapid rotators, or its emission in hosts is usually small. Limitations: low resolution and a pseudo-continuum that depends on gravity; the calibration uses field stars; no inclination test was possible because archive v sin i is missing or unreliable.

citations.reason: TESS sector 56-107 CPV survey: per-star periods, rapid-rotator flags, blind CPV labels, amplitudes and the 2-minute target table with Gaia IDs and height above the main sequence.
BANYAN Sigma age classes and the matched rapid-rotator window used as covariates and sample definition.
S1-S55-only stars, periods and counted CPV labels used as a replication sample.
That result found normal X-ray coronae in CPV hosts; we find normal chromospheric H-alpha at fixed age, colour, period and height.
Its clump model puts clumps in most young rapid rotators; equal H-alpha in hosts and non-hosts agrees with plasma common to all young rapid rotators.
Host persistence over years, used to argue that Gaia 2014-2017 spectra see most TESS hosts in their host state.
Hosts flare 1.6 times more than matched rotators; one of the few host-specific activity differences.
States that no archive v sin i exists for an inclination test; we confirm that GALAH DR4 v sin i is also not usable.
Corotation-ratio (x) model of the CPV rate; we use an x_sb proxy.
Earlier test of a circumstellar signal (infrared excess) in CPV hosts.
Theory of a thermal hydrogen screen at corotation; our result bounds the time-averaged hydrogen emission of hosts.

Bouma et al. 2026: corotating plasma clump H-alpha emission in TIC 300651846 (about 60% and 10% of the stellar EW on different nights) and the LP 12-502 limit; these set the emitting states that we test.
